findings.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages calculation in admin-group.js.es6: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 creates a phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, leaving 'next' enabled on the last real page and allowing navigation to an empty member list; should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

Public group members page (group/members.hbs and groups_controller.rb) silently truncates to 50 members with no pagination UI, a data-visibility regression since previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups returned 200; the old TODO comment was deleted without replacement

Adding a nonexistent username via admin groups add_members is a silent success: unknown names are skipped, success_json is still rendered, the client ignores the returned promise, does not clear the input (TODO acknowledged), and shows no success/error feedback; old specs documenting this behavior were deleted without a new contract test

PATCH changes:{add/delete} incremental-membership API removed from admin groups update with no replacement or deprecation; existing consumers PATCHing with changes now get a 200 success while nothing changes, and all five old specs covering incremental add/delete semantics were deleted

Spec for removing members from automatic groups uses xhr :put instead of the correct DELETE verb for the remove_member route, so the actual DELETE route for member removal is never exercised anywhere in the suite and a routing mistake would ship undetected

Server-side pagination parameters in groups_controller.rb are unvalidated: limit and offset accept arbitrary values, so a direct request with offset=-1 produces a negative OFFSET SQL clause causing a 500, and an uncapped limit allows pulling the entire member list in one query; client-side clamping is not server-side validation

Pagination logic in admin-group.js.es6 has boundary bugs: when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, totalPages is off by one showing an unreachable extra page; when user_count is not a multiple, next() clamps offset to user_count and the server returns an empty member list on the last page

GroupsController public members endpoint now caps ALL groups at 50 members via unconditional limit, while the only public consumer (group/members.hbs template) sends no offset parameter or paging controls, so regular users can only ever see the first 50 members of any group

Test in groups_controller_spec.rb exercises the wrong endpoint: xhr :put, :remove_member issues a PUT that routes to add_members, so the test passes for the wrong reason and provides zero coverage that remove_member blocks automatic groups

add_members silently swallows unknown usernames (User.find_by_username returns nil and the username is dropped with no error) and the client never clears the user-selector input after submit, so admins get a success response with stale input and no indication some names were not added

remove_member replaces the previous Group#remove code path with a raw association delete (group.users.delete(user_id)), silently skipping any membership side effects performed by Group#remove or GroupUser destroy callbacks

Unrelated cosmetic churn not traceable to the requirement: re-indentation of the shared user-selector-autocomplete template, whitespace-only changes to admin-group-selector.hbs, no-op ilike→ILIKE casing change, and blank-line/method-reordering in controllers, inflating the diff surface

Admin groups update/create changed from nested `group: {...}` payload to flat top-level params, breaking existing API consumers and silently flipping `visible` to false when `params[:visible]` is nil, with the PATCH incremental `changes` contract deleted without version bump
GET /groups/:group_id/members response shape changed from a bare JSON array to `{members, meta}` without versioning, breaking consumers that iterate the root array
`GET /admin/groups/users` route deleted, causing 404s for existing callers with no backward-compat shim

admin-group.js totalPages calculation uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` instead of `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`, producing a phantom empty page (e.g. 100 users, limit 50 → 3 pages instead of 2)
Spec for remove_member automatic-group guard uses `xhr :put` which routes to add_members instead of remove_member, leaving the remove_member guard and its user_id path completely unexercised
add_members performs unbounded N+1 queries, calling find_by_username once per username with no cap on list size

add_members silently drops usernames that don't resolve and still returns success_json, so callers can't detect failed adds; UI free-text input with a TODO makes typo'd usernames a silent green response

remove_member uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` on the through-association instead of `group.remove(user)`, potentially bypassing GroupUser callbacks that maintain the denormalized `user_count` counter, causing pagination and displayed totals to desynchronize

Public members endpoint (groups_controller.rb:22-32) response shape silently changed from a serialized top-level array to a wrapped object with meta, breaking existing consumers of GET /groups/:name/members.json

The PATCH incremental-membership API (changes: {add/delete}) was deleted; update now silently ignores the changes param while Rails still routes PATCH to it, causing clients to receive a 200 success while membership mutations are silently dropped

Creation-time membership assignment was removed (admin/groups_controller.rb create + group.js create()) with no explicit acceptance; admins can no longer create a group with initial members in one step, and bulk member removal via the user-selector is no longer possible

Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls (group-members.js.es6 + members.hbs); previously non-automatic groups returned all members, causing a user-visible regression for large groups
admin-group-selector.hbs was gutted to a bare non-functional text input, breaking whatever screen renders the component; unrelated to group memberships and appears to be unreviewed iteration residue

Off-by-one pagination in admin-group.js.es6 totalPages: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 produces a phantom empty page when user_count divides evenly by limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

groups_controller.rb:24 offset = params[:offset].to_i is unclamped; a negative offset like ?offset=-1 reaches PostgreSQL as a negative OFFSET, raising an error and returning a 500 on the public endpoint

The .remove_member spec uses xhr :put for an action routed as DELETE, so controller specs bypass routing and the actual route/verb contract (DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members) is never verified end-to-end

In GroupsController#members, limit/offset params are passed unvalidated to limit().offset(), so negative offset (e.g. offset=-1) produces OFFSET -1 in SQL, causing an unhandled 500 on an unauthenticated-reachable endpoint
In GroupsController#members, limit=0 is not rejected and returns an empty page while still leaking the total count

In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb (context '.update', 'ignore name change on automatic group'), the visible assertion is tautological: the test never establishes visible was false before the request and automatic groups are visible by default, so the test passes even if update ignores all params for automatic groups

The removed '.update' 'incremental' context's coverage for silently skipping non-existent users was deleted without migrating a test for the still-present behavior in Admin::GroupsController#add_members, which also lacks strip handling so 'bob, alice' silently drops 'alice'; neither the unknown-username path nor whitespace handling is tested

In the '.remove_member' context 'cannot remove members from automatic groups', the test uses xhr :put while the new route is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member" and the client sends DELETE, so the route wiring changed in the diff is never exercised and a verb/route misconfiguration would ship undetected

The public GroupsController#members endpoint's response contract changed (flat array to {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} with pagination now applying to all groups) with no test modification; a regression to meta (e.g., missing total) would break client pagination with no failing test

The '.add_members'/'.remove_member' tests hardcode group_id: 1 and depend on Group.find(1) being an automatic group from seed data with no fabricated group or assertion of which group was hit, so the automatic-group guard is validated only against incidental seed state

admin/groups_controller.rb update: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` runs unconditionally, so old callers sending nested payload `{ group: { visible: "true" } }` have their groups silently flipped to invisible (params[:visible] is nil), an unintended permission-relevant change hidden by a 200 success response

admin/groups_controller.rb update: no code path applies `usernames` anymore, so membership changes encoded in `group[:usernames]` by old callers are silently discarded while the API returns success_json

admin/groups_controller.rb create: `group[:usernames]` on POST /admin/groups is now silently ignored, so old callers creating a group with initial members get an empty group with a 200 response and no error indicating members were never added

The API contract change has no expand/contract or dual-accept window — old and new request shapes are never both accepted and there is no deprecation error or fallback, so the transition from nested to top-level params is a silent one-step contract flip

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page (group/members.hbs and groups_controller.rb) silently truncates to 50 members with no pagination UI, a data-visibility regression since previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups returned 200; the old TODO comment was deleted without replacement

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `GroupsController#members`, the new code always applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` for *all* groups, whereas previously non-automatic groups returned the full member list (no limit) and automatic groups defaulted to 200 with offset support. On the client side, the public members route (`discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`) now sets the controller model to the group and calls `model.findMembers()`, and the template (`discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) renders `{{#each m in members}}` but introduces no pagination controls or navigation actions for changing `offset`. With `Group#findMembers` defaulting to `limit: 50, offset: 0`, this means the public group members page will only show the first 50 members unless something else (not in this diff) changes `offset/limit` via params/UI. This is a verifiable data-visibility regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding a nonexistent username via admin groups add_members is a silent success: unknown names are skipped, success_json is still rendered, the client ignores the returned promise, does not clear the input (TODO acknowledged), and shows no success/error feedback; old specs documenting this behavior were deleted without a new contract test

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, which iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record; nonexistent usernames are silently ignored. Regardless of whether any users were found/added, it then calls `group.save` and renders `success_json` on success, so an input consisting entirely of unknown usernames will still look like a successful operation to the client. On the client side, the `addMembers` action just calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` without returning/handling the promise, and explicitly contains `// TODO: should clear the input`, so there is no built-in success/error feedback or input reset in this change. Additionally, the prior spec that asserted silent success when adding non-existent users (under the old PATCH-based API) was removed, and there is no new spec covering the add_members contract for unknown usernames in the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PATCH changes:{add/delete} incremental-membership API removed from admin groups update with no replacement or deprecation; existing consumers PATCHing with changes now get a 200 success while nothing changes, and all five old specs covering incremental add/delete semantics were deleted

adjudication.rationale:
In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#update` was refactored: the prior `request.patch?` branch (`update_patch`) that processed `params[:changes][:add]` / `[:delete]` and modified group membership was removed entirely. The new `update` method only updates `alias_level`, `visible`, and (if not automatic) `name`; it never reads `params[:changes]` or modifies membership. Since Rails routes typically allow PATCH to hit `update`, a client sending `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with only `changes` will now run this `update`, perform no membership changes, and likely still `group.save` successfully, returning `success_json` (200). That is a real backward-incompatible behavior change and can silently succeed.

However, the diff *does* add replacement endpoints (`PUT`/`DELETE` on `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`) via `add_members`/`remove_member`, so the claim “no replacement” is not accurate—though existing PATCH consumers would still break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec for removing members from automatic groups uses xhr :put instead of the correct DELETE verb for the remove_member route, so the actual DELETE route for member removal is never exercised anywhere in the suite and a routing mistake would ship undetected

Server-side pagination parameters in groups_controller.rb are unvalidated: limit and offset accept arbitrary values, so a direct request with offset=-1 produces a negative OFFSET SQL clause causing a 500, and an uncapped limit allows pulling the entire member list in one query; client-side clamping is not server-side validation

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then uses them directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no server-side validation/clamping to ensure `offset >= 0` or to cap `limit`. A request like `?offset=-1` will produce a negative SQL OFFSET (e.g., `OFFSET -1`), which many DBs (notably PostgreSQL) reject, leading to a 500. Likewise, an arbitrarily large (or possibly negative, depending on DB semantics) `limit` can be requested, allowing very large result sets / load. The client-side clamping added in the JS model does not protect the server endpoint from direct requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination logic in admin-group.js.es6 has boundary bugs: when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, totalPages is off by one showing an unreachable extra page; when user_count is not a multiple, next() clamps offset to user_count and the server returns an empty member list on the last page

GroupsController public members endpoint now caps ALL groups at 50 members via unconditional limit, while the only public consumer (group/members.hbs template) sends no offset parameter or paging controls, so regular users can only ever see the first 50 members of any group

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members the diff changes behavior to always apply pagination: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` for all groups, whereas previously only automatic groups were limited/offset (and non-automatic groups returned the full list). On the client side, the public group members page (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 + app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) now loads members via `model.findMembers()` which uses the Group model defaults `limit: 50, offset: 0` and the template simply iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no paging controls shown in the diff. Therefore, with no UI to change `offset`, users will only see the first 50 members of any group by default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test in groups_controller_spec.rb exercises the wrong endpoint: xhr :put, :remove_member issues a PUT that routes to add_members, so the test passes for the wrong reason and provides zero coverage that remove_member blocks automatic groups

adjudication.rationale: The routes change defines `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` and `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, so the *real* HTTP verb for `remove_member` is DELETE. However, the proposed finding claims `xhr :put, :remove_member` would “route to add_members”. In an RSpec controller spec, `xhr :put, :remove_member` invokes the `remove_member` action directly (the symbol determines the action), and the request method doesn’t cause it to dispatch to a different action. Since `remove_member` itself checks `group.automatic` and returns 422 regardless of verb, that test would still cover the automatic-group guard (though it uses the wrong verb). Thus the specific claim that it tests the wrong endpoint / provides zero coverage because it hits `add_members` is not verifiably true from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently swallows unknown usernames (User.find_by_username returns nil and the username is dropped with no error) and the client never clears the user-selector input after submit, so admins get a success response with stale input and no indication some names were not added

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In Admin::GroupsController#add_members the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|; if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end; end` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. Any unknown username yields `nil` and is simply skipped with no error/feedback, so the request can succeed while adding fewer (or zero) users than requested. On the client side, the addMembers action contains an explicit `// TODO: should clear the input` and never resets `this.set("usernames", ...)`, so the user-selector field remains populated after submission, reinforcing the lack of feedback when some names weren’t added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member replaces the previous Group#remove code path with a raw association delete (group.users.delete(user_id)), silently skipping any membership side effects performed by Group#remove or GroupUser destroy callbacks

Unrelated cosmetic churn not traceable to the requirement: re-indentation of the shared user-selector-autocomplete template, whitespace-only changes to admin-group-selector.hbs, no-op ilike→ILIKE casing change, and blank-line/method-reordering in controllers, inflating the diff surface

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include several cosmetic-only changes (indentation in `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs`, whitespace removal in `admin-group-selector.hbs`, `ilike` → `ILIKE` casing, and some blank-line/formatting adjustments). However, these do not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect; they mainly increase diff noise. The proposed finding is therefore a style/review-surface nit rather than a real problem in code behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin groups update/create changed from nested `group: {...}` payload to flat top-level params, breaking existing API consumers and silently flipping `visible` to false when `params[:visible]` is nil, with the PATCH incremental `changes` contract deleted without version bump

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the admin groups API contract. `Admin::GroupsController#create` and `#update` now read flat params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`) instead of the previous nested `params[:group]` payload, and the JS `Discourse.Group#asJSON` was changed accordingly from `{ group: {...} }` to a flat hash, so any existing clients still sending `group: {...}` will no longer work. Additionally, `#update` now unconditionally does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`, which will set `visible` to `false` whenever `visible` is omitted (nil), a concrete behavior change that can unintentionally flip visibility on partial updates. Finally, PATCH/incremental membership updates (`update_patch` with `params[:changes]`) were removed and `update` no longer branches on `request.patch?`, so existing PATCH callers will lose functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET /groups/:group_id/members response shape changed from a bare JSON array to `{members, meta}` without versioning, breaking consumers that iterate the root array

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the response changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` (an object with `members` and `meta`). This is a concrete, backwards-incompatible API shape change for `GET /groups/:group_id/members` (now `/members.json` in the JS) and would break any existing consumer that iterates the root array. The diff shows no versioning or alternate endpoint to preserve the old shape.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `GET /admin/groups/users` route deleted, causing 404s for existing callers with no backward-compat shim

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `get "users"` route under `admin/groups` in `config/routes.rb`, so `/admin/groups/users` would indeed 404 if called. However, the finding asserts impact on “existing callers” without any evidence in the diff that anything still calls this endpoint (no remaining JS/Ruby references shown), and the change appears to be an intentional API refactor (admin membership ops moved to PUT/DELETE `members`, and member listing uses `/groups/:name/members.json`). Without a verifiable in-repo caller, the breakage claim is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group.js totalPages calculation uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` instead of `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`, producing a phantom empty page (e.g. 100 users, limit 50 → 3 pages instead of 2)
matched_golden_ids: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same pagination bug: using Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 adds an extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and suggests using Math.ceil instead, with the same example (100, limit 50 → 3 vs 2).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec for remove_member automatic-group guard uses `xhr :put` which routes to add_members instead of remove_member, leaving the remove_member guard and its user_id path completely unexercised

adjudication.rationale: In this diff the spec file is a controller spec (`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`) using `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`. In Rails controller/functional specs, the second argument (`:remove_member`) directly selects the controller action; it does not route based on HTTP verb the way an integration/request spec would. So `xhr :put` will still execute `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` (not `#add_members`), meaning the automatic-group guard in `remove_member` can still be exercised. While using `:delete` would better mirror the actual route (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`), the proposed finding’s claim that it “routes to add_members instead” is a misreading for this type of spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members performs unbounded N+1 queries, calling find_by_username once per username with no cap on list size

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and for each username executes `User.find_by_username(username)` before `group.add(user)`. This is one DB lookup per username (an N+1 pattern) and there is no explicit limit/cap on how many usernames can be submitted in the request, so a large list will trigger many queries and can be used to cause avoidable load. This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently drops usernames that don't resolve and still returns success_json, so callers can't detect failed adds; UI free-text input with a TODO makes typo'd usernames a silent green response

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code splits the provided `usernames` string and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` succeeds. Unknown/typoed usernames are simply skipped (no error collection). The action then calls `group.save` and, if it succeeds (which it likely will even if nothing was added), returns `render json: success_json`. There is no indication in the response of which usernames failed to resolve, so callers/UI cannot detect partial/total failure. This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` on the through-association instead of `group.remove(user)`, potentially bypassing GroupUser callbacks that maintain the denormalized `user_count` counter, causing pagination and displayed totals to desynchronize

Public members endpoint (groups_controller.rb:22-32) response shape silently changed from a serialized top-level array to a wrapped object with meta, breaking existing consumers of GET /groups/:name/members.json

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`, which returns a top-level JSON array of serialized users, to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, which returns a wrapped object containing `members` and `meta`. This is a concrete, verifiable response-shape change for GET `/groups/:name/members(.json)`. While the in-repo Ember code is updated to use `members`, any existing external consumers expecting an array will break, so the finding describes a real introduced compatibility problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The PATCH incremental-membership API (changes: {add/delete}) was deleted; update now silently ignores the changes param while Rails still routes PATCH to it, causing clients to receive a 200 success while membership mutations are silently dropped

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#update` no longer branches on `request.patch?` and the old `update_patch` implementation that applied `params[:changes][:add/delete]` was removed. Rails REST routing normally maps PATCH to `#update` (same as PUT), and nothing in the diff removes the PATCH route. The new `#update` only reads `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, and `params[:name]` and completely ignores `params[:changes]`. Therefore a client sending `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with only `changes: {add/delete}` will likely get a 200 `success_json` (since `group.save` can succeed with no effective changes) while membership mutations are dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Creation-time membership assignment was removed (admin/groups_controller.rb create + group.js create()) with no explicit acceptance; admins can no longer create a group with initial members in one step, and bulk member removal via the user-selector is no longer possible

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes support for setting initial group members during creation: `Admin::GroupsController#create` no longer reads `params[:group][:usernames]` (or any usernames) and `Discourse.Group#create` now posts only `asJSON()` containing `name/alias_level/visible` (no usernames). The admin UI also now only renders the member management UI under `{{#if id}}`, meaning you must create/save the group first before adding members. Additionally, the previous member management used a `user-selector` bound to `usernames` derived from `members` plus `saveWithUsernames/createWithUsernames`, which could implicitly support bulk removals by editing the selector list; that flow is gone and replaced with per-member remove links (`removeMember`) and a separate add-members action, so bulk removal via the selector is no longer available. This is a real, verifiable loss of functionality introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls (group-members.js.es6 + members.hbs); previously non-automatic groups returned all members, causing a user-visible regression for large groups

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit` (default 50) and `offset` for *all* groups, whereas previously only `automatic?` groups were limited and non-automatic groups returned the full member list. On the client, `group-members.js.es6` now sets the controller model to the group and calls `model.findMembers()`, and the template `group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}` (the group model’s `members` property set by `findMembers`). However, no pagination controls/actions are added to the public group members page/template in this diff, so users will only ever see the first page (50) with no UI to navigate further—i.e., a silent truncation/regression for large non-automatic groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group-selector.hbs was gutted to a bare non-functional text input, breaking whatever screen renders the component; unrelated to group memberships and appears to be unreviewed iteration residue

adjudication.rationale: The diff for `admin-group-selector.hbs` only removes surrounding blank lines; the template content remains a single `<input type="text">` both before and after. There is no functional change introduced here, so the claim that it was “gutted” and made non-functional is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one pagination in admin-group.js.es6 totalPages: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 produces a phantom empty page when user_count divides evenly by limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages returns Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 (when user_count != 0). If user_count is exactly divisible by limit (e.g., user_count=50, limit=50 from Group model defaults/meta), this computes 2 pages even though there is only 1 page of results, creating a phantom empty last page. The correct computation for total pages is Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (with the existing 0-case guard).

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb:24 offset = params[:offset].to_i is unclamped; a negative offset like ?offset=-1 reaches PostgreSQL as a negative OFFSET, raising an error and returning a 500 on the public endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping to `>= 0`, so a request like `?offset=-1` will result in an ActiveRecord query with a negative OFFSET. PostgreSQL rejects negative OFFSET values (or Rails may raise), which can surface as an unhandled exception and a 500 on this public endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The .remove_member spec uses xhr :put for an action routed as DELETE, so controller specs bypass routing and the actual route/verb contract (DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members) is never verified end-to-end

In GroupsController#members, limit/offset params are passed unvalidated to limit().offset(), so negative offset (e.g. offset=-1) produces OFFSET -1 in SQL, causing an unhandled 500 on an unauthenticated-reachable endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping/validation. If a request supplies `offset=-1`, `to_i` yields -1 and ActiveRecord will emit an `OFFSET -1` (which PostgreSQL rejects with an error), leading to an exception/500 since nothing rescues it here. This endpoint is in the non-admin GroupsController and only gates on `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`, so it can be reachable without authentication for visible groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In GroupsController#members, limit=0 is not rejected and returns an empty page while still leaking the total count

adjudication.rationale: The diff does allow `limit=0` because `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` has no validation, and `group.users...limit(0)` will return an empty `members` list while still returning `meta.total`. However, `meta.total` is explicitly included in the response for *all* limits (not just 0), and access is still gated by `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`. So this isn’t a clear defect/security leak introduced by `limit=0`; it’s either an acceptable API behavior (count-only query) or a design choice, not a verifiable “problem” in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb (context '.update', 'ignore name change on automatic group'), the visible assertion is tautological: the test never establishes visible was false before the request and automatic groups are visible by default, so the test passes even if update ignores all params for automatic groups

The removed '.update' 'incremental' context's coverage for silently skipping non-existent users was deleted without migrating a test for the still-present behavior in Admin::GroupsController#add_members, which also lacks strip handling so 'bob, alice' silently drops 'alice'; neither the unknown-username path nor whitespace handling is tested

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the prior PATCH-based incremental membership update (and its spec coverage) with new Admin::GroupsController#add_members that does `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username) ... end` without trimming per-username whitespace. This means an input like "bob, alice" will iterate " alice" and fail to find that user, silently skipping it. The removed spec context previously covered silent skipping of non-existent users, and the new specs shown only cover adding valid comma-joined usernames without spaces; no migrated test covers the unknown-username path or whitespace handling for add_members.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the '.remove_member' context 'cannot remove members from automatic groups', the test uses xhr :put while the new route is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member" and the client sends DELETE, so the route wiring changed in the diff is never exercised and a verb/route misconfiguration would ship undetected
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that the test calls remove_member with xhr :put while the route is defined as a DELETE to groups#remove_member, meaning the test doesn’t exercise the actual route/method and could miss a verb/route mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The public GroupsController#members endpoint's response contract changed (flat array to {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} with pagination now applying to all groups) with no test modification; a regression to meta (e.g., missing total) would break client pagination with no failing test

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, ...)` (a flat array) to a JSON object with `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, and the JS client was updated to consume `result.meta`/`result.members`. However, the finding’s core complaint is about missing/unchanged tests for this public endpoint and the possibility of a future regression (e.g. missing `meta.total`) not being caught. That is a test coverage concern and speculative risk, not a concrete, verifiable defect introduced by the diff. Also, no `GroupsController` spec is shown/modified here, so “no test modification” is not directly verifiable as a regression-causing issue in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The '.add_members'/'.remove_member' tests hardcode group_id: 1 and depend on Group.find(1) being an automatic group from seed data with no fabricated group or assertion of which group was hit, so the automatic-group guard is validated only against incidental seed state

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the new tests under `context ".add_members"` call `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, ...` and expect a 422 to validate the automatic-group guard. The diff shows no fabrication or lookup of an automatic group for `id=1` within the spec, so the test’s correctness depends on pre-existing/seeded state (that `Group.find(1)` exists and is automatic). This is the same pattern already visible in the diff for `context ".update"` (`id: 1`) and appears intended for the new `.remove_member` tests as well. That makes the test brittle and only incidentally validates the guard depending on environment setup, which is a real defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb update: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` runs unconditionally, so old callers sending nested payload `{ group: { visible: "true" } }` have their groups silently flipped to invisible (params[:visible] is nil), an unintended permission-relevant change hidden by a 200 success response

admin/groups_controller.rb update: no code path applies `usernames` anymore, so membership changes encoded in `group[:usernames]` by old callers are silently discarded while the API returns success_json

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally removes `group.usernames` handling from `Admin::GroupsController#update` and moves membership changes to new endpoints `add_members`/`remove_member` (with matching new routes and JS model methods). The updated frontend no longer sends `group[:usernames]` on save/create (`Group#asJSON` drops it; `saveWithUsernames/createWithUsernames` removed). So while it’s true that a legacy client sending `group[usernames]` would now be ignored (and `update` could still return `success_json` if the group saves), that backward-compatibility concern depends on callers outside this diff and appears to be an intended API change, not a verifiable defect within the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb create: `group[:usernames]` on POST /admin/groups is now silently ignored, so old callers creating a group with initial members get an empty group with a 200 response and no error indicating members were never added

The API contract change has no expand/contract or dual-accept window — old and new request shapes are never both accepted and there is no deprecation error or fallback, so the transition from nested to top-level params is a silent one-step contract flip

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the admin groups create/update request shape from nested params (params[:group][...]) to top-level params (params[:name], params[:alias_level], params[:visible]) in both the Rails controller and the Ember model (Group#asJSON, Group#create/save). Within this diff, all in-repo callers are updated accordingly (tests and JS), and there’s no remaining code shown that still sends the old nested shape. The finding asserts a defect due to lack of backward-compatibility/deprecation, but that’s a process/API-stability concern rather than a verifiable bug introduced by this diff unless there are other clients/callers (not shown) that must still work.
